title: Check if Array is Sorted
statement:
Write a function that checks if an array of integers `nums` is sorted in non-decreasing (ascending) order.

Return `true` if it is sorted, and `false` otherwise. An array with less than two elements is considered sorted.

examples.explanation: The array elements are strictly increasing.
Element 3 is larger than its successor 2.

editorial.approach: Iterate from index 1 to n - 1. If nums[i] < nums[i - 1], the array is not sorted. Return false. If loop ends without trigger, return true.

hints: An array is sorted if every element is greater than or equal to the element before it.
Start your loop from index 1 and check if `nums[i] < nums[i - 1]`.
If you find any index where this condition is true, return false immediately. Otherwise, return true after the loop.

bruteForceSolution.explanation: Create a copy of the array, sort it, and compare it element-by-element with the original array.

optimizedSolution.explanation: Perform a single pass from the second element. Check if the current element is smaller than the previous element. If so, return false.

interviewExplanation: A brute-force sort comparison takes O(n log n) time and O(n) space. We optimize it to O(n) time and O(1) space by checking if adjacent elements satisfy the sorting constraint (`nums[i] >= nums[i-1]`) in a single pass.
